subject: Request: SLA exception for batched-inference operational guardrail
messages:
From: Ellis Moran <ellis@brightline.io>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, procurement@optimax.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: SLA exception request for batched inference workloads

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — the performance looked promising. Before we move forward with procurement, the operations team asked whether Redwood can accommodate a narrow SLA exception for our batched-inference profile.

Context: Brightline runs large nightly batch jobs that spike GPU utilization and sometimes trigger preemption/eviction on shared pools. Those windows are predictable (01:00–04:00 PT) and account for ~12% of our monthly token volume, but they heavily affect our tail latency during the window.

Ask: would Redwood consider the following carveout in the standard SLA template?
- For batched windows (nightly 01:00–04:00 PT), lower the uptime requirement to 99.90 (from your standard 99.95) for the affected host pool.
- Cap monthly service credits tied to that carveout at 5% of monthly invoice.
- Explicit maintenance/eviction carveout for preemption events initiated by cloud provider or autoscaler during those windowed batch runs.

We're open to a short pilot (1–2 months) and happy to provide the batch job traces (I attached a CSV with representative metrics). If feasible, please confirm what metrics or contract language you’d need so our legal team can prepare redlines.

Appreciate it — we want to move quickly if we can get alignment on the remedy cap.

Best,
Ellis Moran
Director of Infrastructure, Brightline
ellis@brightline.io

Attachment: batched-inference-metrics.csv (csv, 42KB)
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Moran <ellis@brightline.io>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA exception request for batched inference workloads

Ellis — thanks for the clear note and for sending the metrics. I reviewed the CSV quickly and it confirms the predictable nightly spike. We can absolutely discuss an operational carveout for batched windows, but want to be explicit about trade-offs so procurement and legal have a clean redline.

High-level proposal from our side:
- Provisional uptime: 99.90 for identified batched host pools during the specified window, with automatic reversion to standard 99.95 outside that window.
- Monthly remedy cap: capped at 5% of monthly invoice for failures attributable to preemption/eviction during the batch window (you proposed this already — we can accept with clarifying language).
- Maintenance/external event carveout: we will exclude cloud-provider-initiated maintenance and preemptions from SLA eligibility provided we give 72-hour notice where practicable.
- Observability: Redwood Console will surface token-level latency and the specific request buckets we consider for the carveout; we'll provide a shared dashboard for the pilot.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Aditya and I draft the contract language and a short addendum that defines the windows + remedy calculation.
2) Legal (laura) will add the insurance/indemnity language and confirm the cap is applied only to remedies, not to other remedy types.
3) Pilot: 45-day pilot where we flag relevant traffic and run canary routing to a dedicated pool. If stability is acceptable we fold the addendum into the order form.

If that sounds good, can we schedule a 30-minute call to walk legal/procurement through the exact wording? I'm free Wed 11/4 3pm PT or Thu 11/5 9am PT.

Thanks — Jonas
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Ellis — quick technical + commercial note from the product side. We agree the carveout is reasonable for predictable, high-density batch windows. A couple specifics to smooth contracting and run the pilot:

Technical guardrails
- We recommend routing night-batch traffic to a dedicated pool (either Dedicated or pinned hosted pool) to isolate performance impact. That reduces cross-tenant eviction risk.
- For the remedy calculation, we should use measured request-level availability as reported by the console (p95/p99 latency buckets) and correlate with your supplied traces.

Commercial wording we will propose
- Define the carveout precisely as: "Availability measurements for requests flagged as \u2018batched-window\u2019 by mutual agreement during 01:0002:00 PT each night (date range) will be excluded from standard SLA calculations." (We will draft the precise flagging mechanism in the addendum.)
- Remedy cap: 5% monthly invoice, applied as account credit within 30 days of validated claim.

I'll attach a CSV with the cluster-level metrics we pulled (same file you sent, normalized). If you want, Marissa from CS can run an onboarding doc with your ops team to wire the dashboard and the request tagging.

Aditya Rao
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Thanks — this aligns well with our expectations. A couple quick items from procurement/legal:
- Please send a redline addendum we can review. If possible, include the exact tagging/flagging language so our SREs know how requests will be counted.
- We need a DocuSign-ready PDF by next week to hit our internal procurement window.

I'll block the 3pm PT Wed slot you suggested for a short call; if something changes I'll let you know. Once laura sees the addendum we'll get our counsel in the loop.

Best,
Ellis
